AuthEffect.description:
What an enforcement point does to a request that reaches it.

``UNKNOWN`` is a first-class answer, not a placeholder: an enforcement we
can see but cannot interpret must say so, because the alternative is
leaving the endpoint reading as unprotected (§5.2.9).
AuthEffect.title: AuthEffect

AuthEvidence.description:
One enforcement point that gates — or could gate — this endpoint (§5.2.9).

Every claim carries its source, and every construct that *could* gate a
request is recorded here whether or not its effect could be determined.
That is what makes the claim rule on :class:`EndpointAuth` safe: a rule we
failed to read is present as ``resolution=opaque`` rather than absent.

**Reader migration (pre-1.13.0 artifacts):** records written before the
enforcement model carry no ``effect``/``resolution``, so they default to
``unknown``/``resolved`` — honest about what was recorded (the effect was
never stored) while preserving the claim those artifacts were written with.

active.description: False when present in source but not in effect
active.title: Active

authorities.description: Authorities required, when distinct from roles
authorities.title: Authorities

effect.description: What this does to a request that reaches it

expression.description: Raw access expression / SpEL, preserved verbatim
expression.title: Expression

http_method.description: Verb restriction; None means the rule applies to every verb

inactive_reason.description: Why it is not in effect, e.g. 'disabled in chain' — required when inactive
inactive_reason.title: Inactive Reason

pattern.description: Path pattern this is scoped to; '{?}' means read but unresolvable
pattern.title: Pattern

AuthEvidence.title: AuthEvidence

AuthEvidenceKind.description:
What kind of construct enforces (or could enforce) access (§5.2.9).

The first three are declarative sources; the rest are enforcement points
that gate requests without a security-framework rule behind them. All are
framework-neutral by construction — a FastAPI ``Security(...)`` dependency
or an Express middleware maps onto the same vocabulary (goal 9).
AuthEvidenceKind.title: AuthEvidenceKind

AuthMechanism.description:
One authentication mechanism configured on the service that serves this endpoint.

A custom filter is only ever promoted past ``CUSTOM_FILTER`` on evidence
inside the filter itself — naming a mechanism from a class name would be
exactly the fabricated security fact §12 forbids.

active.description: False when present in source but not in effect
active.title: Active

detail.description: Raw source text or filter class name
detail.title: Detail

inactive_reason.description: Why it is not in effect, e.g. 'disabled in chain' — required when inactive
inactive_reason.title: Inactive Reason

AuthMechanism.title: AuthMechanism

AuthMechanismKind.description: How a caller proves identity — distinct from what it is then allowed to do.
AuthMechanismKind.title: AuthMechanismKind

AuthResolution.description:
How completely an enforcement point was read.

``OPAQUE`` is what withholds an endpoint's claim (§5.2.9): the construct
was detected but its effect or scope could not be determined.
AuthResolution.title: AuthResolution

CalleeUnboundReason.description:
Why a call node's target has no interior in the graph (§5.4.2 T5).

These are *not* failures to report as errors. A Lombok accessor has no
source body by construction; a JDK method is not the system's code. The
reason exists so a consumer can render "no source to analyse, because X"
rather than a node that dead-ends for no stated cause — which is
indistinguishable from a hole in the map, and is what made a correct
extraction read as data loss (P10).
CalleeUnboundReason.title: CalleeUnboundReason

Confidence.description: Confidence tiers for recovered facts (§5.4). Ordered EXACT > HIGH > HEURISTIC > NONE.
Confidence.title: Confidence

Endpoint.description: One REST endpoint of one service within a snapshot.

request_schema.description: Field-level @RequestBody shape (§5.2.7); None = no body or pre-1.6

Endpoint.title: Endpoint

EndpointAuth.description:
Structured authorization state of an endpoint (§5.2.9).

``authenticated`` is tri-state (P10): True/False are *claims backed by
fully-read enforcement*; None means honestly unknown — never defaulted to
False. The distinction between None and False is load-bearing: None says
"we did not read everything that guards this", False says "we read it all
and nothing guards this". Collapsing them is the failure mode this model
exists to prevent.

``denied`` refines the True case rather than replacing it. ``denyAll()``
admits nobody, so "a request must be authenticated to pass" is still true
of it — but a route no caller can reach is not the same fact as a working
protected route, and rendering the two identically tells an auditor a dead
endpoint is live. It is a separate boolean, not a fourth value of
``authenticated``, so every existing reader of the tri-state keeps working.

authorities.description: Authorities required, when the rule names authorities rather than roles
authorities.title: Authorities

denied.description: A read rule denies EVERY caller (denyAll); the endpoint is unreachable
denied.title: Denied

evidence.description: Every enforcement point in scope — read or not (§5.2.9)
evidence.title: Evidence

mechanism.description: Framework family, e.g. 'spring-security'; see mechanisms[] for how auth works
mechanism.title: Mechanism

mechanisms.title: Mechanisms

ShapeKind.description:
The recovered wire-shape node kinds (§5.2.7). ``unresolved``/``cycle``/
``truncated`` are honest terminals — never fabricated fields (P10).
ShapeKind.title: ShapeKind

ShapeOrigin.description:
Which evidence the shape was read from (§5.2.7, amended 2026-08-05).

``declared`` is the signature — the strongest evidence, and the only one
used until a raw wrapper (`public HttpEntity query(...)`) leaves nothing to
unwrap. ``return_expression`` means the payload came from what the handler
returns, which is still symbolic truth but rests on a weaker premise: one
return path standing for the whole contract. P7 keeps the two legible
rather than blending them.
ShapeOrigin.title: ShapeOrigin

SourceAnchor.description:
A file + line range in the text that was actually analyzed.

For preprocessed files (delombok) the anchor refers to the generated
variant — source-on-demand serves that same text, so anchors and served
source stay aligned by construction (§5.3).

file.description: Path relative to the service build root
file.title: File

Whether an anchor refers to original repo text or a generated variant (§5.3).

``GENERATED`` marks preprocessor output (e.g. delombok'ed Java) — the text
that was actually analyzed, served by source-on-demand with a badge.
SourceVariant.title: SourceVariant

TargetKind.description:
What a stitched edge lands on (§5.4.2) — the three target kinds that
keep partial coverage honest, plus the explicit undetermined fact (P10).

TokenPropagation.description:
WHETHER the caller's credentials cross this call (§5.2.11 T4).

``auth_propagation`` names the mechanism when there is one; this says
whether there is one at all, and — the part a nullable string could not
express — distinguishes "we proved it does not" from "we could not tell".
The difference decides whether a downstream 401 is a finding or a shrug.

A recovered request/response shape (§5.2.7): the wire contract, walked
from in-CPG type structure with honest terminals.

UnopenableCallCount.description:
Call sites sharing one reason for having no interior (§5.4.2 T5).

Deliberately a count per reason rather than a bare total: "12 calls you
cannot open" reads as damage, while "10 Lombok accessors, 2 JDK methods"
reads as what it is — code that was never the system's to show.

call_count.description: Call sites in this endpoint's flow with this reason
call_count.title: Call Count

UnopenableCallCount.title: UnopenableCallCount

description:
Everything the endpoint workspace needs in one read (§11 Phase 2.8).

1.11.0 (additive): replaces the client-side compose of endpoint +
service-wide remote edges. The ICFG stays its own fetch (it is large) and
source stays on demand (§5.3) — ``touched_files`` carries names, never
content.

**Reading the empty lists.** Each one has a flag that says whether empty
means 'none' or 'not known', because on their own they cannot be told
apart (P10):

* ``outbound`` — ``stitched=False`` means the stitcher has not run, so
  empty is 'not yet'.
* ``touched_files`` and ``unopenable_calls`` — both are DERIVED from the
  ICFG, so ``icfg_available=False`` makes empty 'not known'. Without that
  reading, an endpoint with no flow graph reports the same shape as one
  whose every call opens cleanly.

icfg_schema_version.description: 1.12.0: the schema version of the ICFG `touched_files` and `unopenable_calls` were derived from; None when no ICFG exists. Reason codes arrived in 1.12.0, so an older graph yields an empty `unopenable_calls` that means 'not recorded', not 'none' (P10).
icfg_schema_version.title: Icfg Schema Version

unopenable_calls.description: 1.12.0 (§5.4.2 T5): how many call sites in this endpoint's flow have no interior to open, by reason. This is the endpoint-level honesty surface — `analysis_coverage` sizes reachability system-wide and the coverage report's unresolved counts cover only cross-service edges, so intra-service unopenable calls were counted NOWHERE per endpoint. Derived from the ICFG, so read it with `icfg_available`: empty with a graph present means every call opens; empty WITHOUT one means not known. `icfg_schema_version` distinguishes a pre-1.12.0 graph, which carried no reasons to count.
unopenable_calls.title: Unopenable Calls
